root.name: Richter-Veresov Attack: Richter Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nc3 d5 3. Bg5 Bf5 4. f3

overview: After 1.d4 Nf6 2.Nc3 d5 3.Bg5 Bf5 White plays 4.f3 to prepare e4 and keep the Bg5 supported, with a pawn centre to follow. Black can reply 4...Nbd7, 4...Bg6 or 4...c6, and answers e4 with ...dxe4 fxe4 and ...Bxe4. It is a less common idea than 4.Bxf6 or 4.e3.

white_ideas.idea: Push e4 with f3 support and open the centre
Keep the Bg5 and pressure Black kingside

black_ideas.idea: Trade the centre with ...dxe4 and develop the Bf5

typical_structures.structure: White pawn centre d4/e4/f3 vs flexible Black development

character.notes: f3 supports e4 and keeps the Bg5, so play stays about the centre with no forced sacrifices.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

soundness.notes: Sound, a modest anti-Bf5 idea; Black equalises with ...Nbd7/...c6 or ...dxe4.

structure.notes: The d4 and e-pawn tension after f3 and e4 leaves the centre undecided.

approach.notes: A sideline within the Richter-Veresov, itself a respectable but secondary choice.

level.notes: Plans and tactics around e4 and the Bg5 pin; little deep theory.

character.reason: Neither clearly solid nor forcing; f3 is slightly loosening.

soundness.reason: f3 is a normal if slightly slow Veresov idea.

structure.reason: Tension around d4 and e4 with the centre not yet decided.

approach.reason: A sideline of a respectable opening rather than an unused one.

level.reason: Needs central plans, not heavy memory.

plans.reason: White aims for e4 and a broad pawn centre.
